title: Paying the Price, in Euros

source.title: How is the US-Israeli war on Iran causing havoc in Europe?
source.note: published 10-25 14:47 (page metadata, zone not stated); the newest hit on an object with a live window in the 10-25 sweep. An explainer — the roster names explainers as AJ's cuttable form. Non-US horizon, flagged. Read in full via the cloud fetch; reductions filed, no quotation over fifteen words. Three sub-headings: How has Europe's position changed? · Have European bases been used? · High prices and protest

object.label: H1 — the Russian diesel deal (PG01 layer 1): the price leg (H1c) read from outside the US horizon — the crunch as Europe's bill (diesel doubled, the import bill +€106bn, Brent above $100), with the deal on the page at ¶31 as Washington's relief; the Strait (H6) at ¶19 and ¶27 and the next offensive (slate01's force) at ¶1, ¶8, ¶11–¶13 marked

zAxis.pos: prices come down by the deal
zAxis.neg: they do not — the price is set by the Strait and the next strike, and Europe's relief is asked of Europe's own stocks

transformNote: the shadow is the deal's promise (prices coming down by Russian diesel); the page reads the same price from Europe, where it is a doubled diesel bill, a 140% gas rise, an extra €106bn of imports and a Brent that has not been under $100 since spring — and where the deal appears once, in one sentence, as Washington's two asks: release your emergency diesel stocks, and accept Russian diesel back on the market. The page's own object is Europe's turn against the next strike; the cut reads that turn as the price's politics and marks the force lines

split.note: one station, two planes: the price (the article, the Commission, the two academics: 8–18, every line dated and denominated in euros or dollars) and the politics of the price (the ministers, the spokesman, the sociologist: 30–72). The page oscillates by speaker, not within one — except von der Leyen, whose February and October lines are one migration: 'renewed hope' → 'paying the price'

scoreboard.zRule: every line carries a z, inferred where implied (Sailor 2026-10-13); inferred lines are marked zInferred with a zWhy

lines.quote: How is the US-Israeli war on Iran causing havoc in Europe? — rising energy costs and protests are sharpening European opposition to renewed attacks
lines.note: THE DOOR: 'havoc' is the page's word; the dek joins the price and the force in one sentence — the cost is the cause of the opposition. The object (the price) and the force (the next strike) enter together
lines.zWhy: a price that sharpens opposition to the next strike is a price read as still rising

lines.quote: several Western European states oppose a renewed war as soaring oil prices deepen Europe's cost-of-living crisis
lines.note: the thesis: the price as the politics. 'Soaring' is the only verdict word; the rest is placement
lines.zWhy: soaring oil prices deepening a crisis are prices not coming down

lines.quote: Germany and the UK, which first stayed quiet on the bombardment, now call for diplomacy to end a war that has disrupted global oil supplies
lines.note: MIGRATION, two governments in one sentence: quiet in February, diplomacy in October — the page's structure stated as a fact
lines.zWhy: two capitals turned by a disrupted supply read the supply as the mover

lines.quote: ongoing energy disruption is raising household costs as winter approaches, adding to living-standards protests across European capitals
lines.note: THE CLOCK: winter. The first of four lines on the page that date the price forward
lines.zWhy: household costs rising into winter are a price with a season, not a cure

lines.quote: Baghaei recalls Merz in June 2025 — 'the dirty work Israel is doing for all of us' — against Berlin's warnings now
lines.note: a party to the war scoring a chancellor's migration with the chancellor's own words, as-of June 2025. Frame, not the price; surface-bound (reads Berlin's stance, not the bill). The quotation is the record; the use is the verdict
lines.zWhy: a 'dirty work' line recalled is Berlin's turn read as the cost of the work

lines.quote: Schiller: reason dragged toward an abyss by madness
lines.note: denominated — the literary verdict; the object is nowhere in the line. The page's first denominated voice is a foreign ministry's
lines.zWhy: an abyss is a price read as a consequence of madness, unsized

lines.quote: the February 28 statement did not condemn the opening attacks; nearly eight months in, European governments explicitly warn against another campaign
lines.note: dated: February 28 → nearly eight months. The migration measured in months, by the article
lines.zWhy: a warning that took eight months reads the eighth month's price as the reason

lines.quote: further escalation would create nothing but losers and hurt hydrocarbon prices
lines.note: the challenge predicate, re-reported: the next strike priced into hydrocarbons — the same Barrot line the 10-23 cut scored (aj_2026-10-23 ¶5); second sighting, same words
lines.zWhy: a strike that hurts hydrocarbon prices is a price whose next move is up

lines.quote: the eight-nation group will urge both sides to show the utmost restraint — another regional escalation is unaffordable
lines.note: 'unaffordable' — the minister's frame prices the strike without a number; the Istanbul format restated (the 10-23 candidate)
lines.zWhy: an unaffordable escalation is a bill already too large

lines.quote: Sánchez: the campaign is illegal, unjust and unjustified — tied to Europe's rising economic costs
lines.note: the oscillation zone's top: three adjectives and then the cost. Pattern: the verdict precedes the object (Protocol destruction mode: verdict over object); the economic clause keeps it on the page
lines.zWhy: a war called unjust because it costs is the price read as the argument

lines.quote: Britain first withheld permission, then allowed US use of its bases for limited defensive strikes, later expanded to missile sites threatening Hormuz shipping
lines.note: H6 TOUCHED — marked: the Strait as a target set (missile sites threatening shipping) and Britain's authorisation as the instrument. The record, three steps, undated on the page
lines.zWhy: bases opened for strikes on sites threatening Hormuz shipping read the Strait as not open

lines.quote: Spain refused use of Rota and Morón and closed its airspace to US aircraft involved in the war
lines.note: the record: a government's act, two bases and an airspace — the page's lowest-Dia line; Trump's reply ('terrible', 'nothing to do with Spain') is at ¶22, filed in the objects pass, not scored here
lines.zWhy: an airspace closed to the war reads neither way on the price

lines.quote: what was initially a diplomatic disagreement grows more direct; leaders might openly challenge Trump and limit support
lines.note: the academic's frame on the alliance; the price is the premise, not the line
lines.zWhy: a disagreement growing direct is the cost read as the reason to say so

lines.quote: von der Leyen in February: 'renewed hope for the people of Iran'; by October 16: households and industry are paying the price
lines.note: MIGRATION inside one voice across eight months — 'renewed hope' (February, after Khamenei's death) → 'paying the price' (10-16). The page's best demonstration of Rule 5, and the cut's title
lines.zWhy: hope in February and a price in October is a cure that did not arrive

lines.quote: Europe's imported fossil-fuel bill up €106 billion; gas prices up about 140 percent since late February; diesel prices doubled
lines.note: THE PRICE, IN EUROS: three register numbers from the Commission — the bill, the gas, the diesel. 'Doubled' is the H1c figure from outside the US horizon; the most denominated-in-currency, least denominated-in-verdict line on the page
lines.zWhy: a diesel price doubled is the price leg read as not come down

lines.quote: Brent $72.48 on February 27, $126.41 at the end of April, still above $100; Gulf supply disruption and Hormuz shipping restrictions
lines.note: THE RECORD, DATED: the benchmark's path with three prices and two dates; H6 named as the cause ('Hormuz shipping restrictions') — marked. The lowest-Dia line on the page
lines.zWhy: a Brent above $100 since spring is a price the deal has not moved

lines.quote: the war's economic toll will worsen energy markets and push prices up as Europe enters winter — there is the economic interest as well
lines.note: the forward price, dated (winter), by the reader; 'as well' — the economic interest named beside the political one
lines.zWhy: prices pushed up into winter are the price's next move read as up

lines.quote: the Gulf is a hub for nitrogen fertilisers; urea up roughly 70 percent; shipping firms face higher insurance premiums and longer reroutes
lines.note: THE OBJECT IN ANOTHER REGISTER: the crunch as fertiliser (urea +70%), as insurance, as a route — Sailor's frame (10-16): one object through many registers. Three sightings in one sentence
lines.zWhy: a crunch that is also fertiliser and insurance is a price wider than the pump

lines.quote: the war has had a direct, measurable and rapid impact on European prices
lines.note: 'measurable' — the reader's claim is that the object can be sized; the sizing is at ¶26–¶27 and ¶29
lines.zWhy: an impact called measurable is a price read as the war's, not the deal's

lines.quote: Washington pressed Europe to release emergency diesel stocks; Trump eased restrictions on Russian diesel to lower prices; Ukraine and its supporters warned the revenue would bolster Moscow
lines.note: H1 ON THE PAGE, ONCE: the deal in one sentence from outside — two asks of Europe (open your stocks; take Russian diesel back) and the Ukrainian objection. The relief is asked of Europe's own reserves; the page does not say whether any were released
lines.zWhy: a relief asked of Europe's own stocks is the deal read as a request, not a delivery

lines.quote: protests over living costs, housing, wages and public services across seven countries — no coordinated movement, but cost-of-living pressures worsened by the war's price rises unite them
lines.note: the price as the street: seven countries named (France, Belgium, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Greece, Albania). The register is the protest; the object is the cause the article assigns
lines.zWhy: protests united by a price are a price not yet relieved

lines.quote: anti-war sentiment is central to the youth protests, alongside anger that military spending takes funds from welfare
lines.note: the sociologist's frame: the protest read for its politics, not its price — surface-bound (right domain, wrong plane)
lines.zWhy: a protest read as anti-war is the price's politics without the price

lines.quote: young protesters fear their future will be stolen — by wars they could be sent to die in, and by global warming
lines.note: 'stolen' — the verdict; the object has left the line for the generation. Oscillation zone
lines.zWhy: a future stolen is a cost read as total and unsized

lines.quote: young people connect wars with genocide, politicised at the protests against what she calls Israel's genocide of the Palestinians
lines.note: the page's last and most denominated line: 'genocide' twice, the price nowhere. Surface-bound; the page closes on the register farthest from its own numbers
lines.zWhy: a war connected to genocide is the price read out of the page
